# Glossary of terms

This glossary contains the most relevant definitions and acronyms of the aviation regulatory framework (EASA, ICAO, national rules) applicable to the Sailplane Pilot Licence (SPL).

**ACC (Area Control Centre)**
: ATS unit that provides area control service to flights under its jurisdiction.

**AD (Airworthiness Directive; Aerodromes)**
: Context-dependent abbreviation: an airworthiness directive is a mandatory requirement to correct an unsafe condition; AD also identifies the aerodromes part of the AIP.

**AESA (Spanish Aviation Safety Agency)**
: Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Aérea: the Spanish authority responsible for overseeing civil aviation safety and applying aviation regulations within its remit.

**AFM (Aircraft Flight Manual)**
: Approved document containing the limitations, procedures and data needed to operate the aircraft.

**AGL (Above Ground Level)**
: Height referred to the surface of the ground below the aircraft or the point considered.

**AIC (Aeronautical Information Circular)**
: Publication containing aeronautical information that does not qualify for inclusion in the AIP or in a NOTAM.

**AIP (Aeronautical Information Publication)**
: Official publication containing aeronautical information of a lasting character essential to air navigation, organised in General (GEN), En-route (ENR) and Aerodromes (AD).

**AIRAC (Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control)**
: System of common dates for publishing significant, foreseeable aeronautical changes and bringing them into effect.

**AIS (Aeronautical Information Service)**
: Service responsible for providing the aeronautical information needed for the safety, regularity and efficiency of air navigation.

**ALERFA (Alert Phase)**
: Phase declared when there is concern for the safety of an aircraft and its occupants.

**ALRS (Alerting Service)**
: ATS service that notifies the appropriate organisations of aircraft in need of search and rescue and cooperates with them.

**AMC (Acceptable Means of Compliance)**
: Non-binding means published by EASA that offer a recognised way of demonstrating compliance with a rule.

**AME (Aero-Medical Examiner)**
: Doctor authorised to carry out examinations and to issue or process aviation medical certificates within their privileges.

**AMP (Aircraft Maintenance Programme)**
: Programme setting out the maintenance tasks and intervals applicable to an aircraft.

**AMSL (Above Mean Sea Level)**
: Altitude referred to mean sea level.

**APP (Approach Control)**
: ATS unit that provides control service to controlled flights arriving at or departing from one or more aerodromes.

**ARC (Airworthiness Review Certificate)**
: Certificate showing that the aircraft has passed the required airworthiness review and remains valid for the applicable period.

**ASM (Airspace Management)**
: Function that manages the use of airspace according to the needs of its different users.

**ATC (Air Traffic Control)**
: Air traffic service intended to prevent collisions and to expedite and maintain an orderly flow of air traffic.

**ATCO (Air Traffic Control Officer)**
: Person licensed to provide air traffic control services within their privileges.

**ATFM (Air Traffic Flow Management)**
: Function that matches air traffic demand to the available capacity of the system.

**ATM (Air Traffic Management)**
: Integrated management of air traffic and airspace through the air traffic services (ATS), airspace management (ASM) and flow management (ATFM).

**ATS (Air Traffic Services)**
: Generic term covering air traffic control (ATC), flight information service (FIS) and alerting service (ALRS).

**ATZ (Aerodrome Traffic Zone)**
: Airspace of defined dimensions established around an aerodrome to protect its traffic.

**AWY (Airway)**
: A control area or part of one established in the form of a corridor.

**CAA (Civil Aviation Authority)**
: Generic name for a State's aviation authority; in Spain, its powers are shared mainly between the DGAC and AESA.

**CAMO (Continuing Airworthiness Management Organisation)**
: Organisation approved to manage the continuing airworthiness of aircraft within its privileges.

**CAO (Combined Airworthiness Organisation)**
: Approved organisation that may exercise maintenance and continuing airworthiness management privileges within the scope of its approval.

**CAVOK (Visibility, cloud and present weather better than prescribed values or conditions)**
: Term used in weather reports that replaces certain visibility, present weather and cloud data when the established conditions are met at the same time: visibility of 10 km or more, no cloud below 5,000 ft and no cumulonimbus, and no significant weather. The name is ICAO's; at the club you will hear the backronym *Ceiling And Visibility OK*, which is not the official name.

**CDR (Conditional Route)**
: ATS route available only when the published conditions are met.

**CIAIAC (Spanish Civil Aviation Accident and Incident Investigation Commission)**
: Comisión de Investigación de Accidentes e Incidentes de Aviación Civil: the official Spanish body responsible for investigating civil aviation accidents and serious incidents for preventive purposes.

**CofA (Certificate of Airworthiness)**
: Document certifying that an aircraft conforms to the approved design and is considered fit for flight while it remains airworthy and meets the applicable requirements.

**CPL (Commercial Pilot Licence)**
: Licence allowing the holder to exercise commercial pilot privileges under the applicable conditions; there is no separate CPL(S) for sailplanes.

**CS (Certification Specifications)**
: Technical specifications used in the certification of aircraft, products and equipment.

**CS-22 (Certification Specifications for Sailplanes and Powered Sailplanes)**
: EASA specifications applicable to the design and certification of sailplanes and powered sailplanes.

**CTA (Control Area)**
: Controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth.

**CTR (Control Zone)**
: Controlled airspace extending upwards from the surface of the earth to a defined upper limit.

**Danger area (D)**
: Airspace of defined dimensions within which activities dangerous to the flight of aircraft may exist at specified times.

**DETRESFA (Distress Phase)**
: Phase declared when there is reasonable certainty that an aircraft and its occupants are threatened by grave and imminent danger and require immediate assistance.

**DGAC (Spanish Directorate General of Civil Aviation)**
: Dirección General de Aviación Civil: the directorate responsible for formulating aviation policy and exercising the functions assigned to it by Spanish law.

**DME (Distance Measuring Equipment)**
: Radio navigation aid that allows an aircraft to determine its slant distance from a ground station.

**EASA (European Union Aviation Safety Agency)**
: European Union agency that develops and oversees the common civil aviation safety framework within its remit.

**EET (Estimated Elapsed Time)**
: The time estimated to be needed to proceed from one reference point to another during a flight.

**ELT (Emergency Locator Transmitter)**
: Aircraft beacon designed to transmit an emergency signal and help locate the aircraft.

**EOBT (Estimated Off-Block Time)**
: The estimated time at which the aircraft will start the movement associated with departure.

**ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival)**
: The time at which the aircraft is expected to arrive at the relevant reference point or place.

**ETD (Estimated Time of Departure)**
: The time at which the aircraft is estimated to begin its departure.

**FCL (Flight Crew Licensing)**
: Part of Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011 on flight crew licences; it is distinct from Part-SFCL, which is specific to sailplanes.

**FE(S) (Flight Examiner (Sailplanes))**
: Examiner authorised to conduct sailplane skill tests and proficiency checks within their privileges.

**FI(S) (Flight Instructor (Sailplanes))**
: Instructor authorised to give flight instruction in sailplanes within their privileges.

**FIC (Flight Information Centre)**
: Unit established to provide flight information service and alerting service.

**FIR (Flight Information Region)**
: Airspace of defined dimensions within which flight information and alerting services are provided.

**FIS (Flight Information Service)**
: Service provided to give advice and information useful for the safe and efficient conduct of flights.

**FISO (Flight Information Service Officer)**
: Staff qualified to provide the flight information service within their privileges.

**FL (Flight Level)**
: Surface of constant pressure expressed in hundreds of feet and related to the standard altimeter setting of 1013.25 hPa.

**FUA (Flexible Use of Airspace)**
: Concept by which airspace is managed as a common resource and allocated dynamically according to needs.

**GM (Guidance Material)**
: Non-binding explanatory material that helps interpret the requirements and the acceptable means of compliance.

**HJ (Sunrise to sunset)**
: Code indicating the period between sunrise and sunset.

**IAIP (Integrated Aeronautical Information Package)**
: Coordinated set of aeronautical information publications and products, including the AIP and its amendments.

**ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization)**
: Specialised agency of the United Nations that sets standards and recommended practices for international civil aviation.

**IFR (Instrument Flight Rules)**
: Rules applicable to flights conducted under instrument flight rules.

**INCERFA (Uncertainty Phase)**
: Phase declared when there is uncertainty about the safety of an aircraft and its occupants.

**IR (Implementing Rules)**
: Legally binding requirements that develop the European civil aviation Basic Regulation.

**LAPL (Light Aircraft Pilot Licence)**
: European licence for certain non-commercial operations with light aircraft, subject to the applicable privileges and limitations.

**LSA (Spanish Aviation Safety Act)**
: Short name of Ley 21/2003, de 7 de julio, de Seguridad Aérea (Aviation Safety Act 21/2003 of 7 July).

**NOTAM (Notice to Airmen)**
: Notice distributed by means of telecommunication containing aeronautical information the timely knowledge of which is essential to flight operations.

**Occurrence reporting system**
: SNS (Sistema de Notificación de Sucesos): the Spanish system for receiving and managing civil aviation occurrence reports for safety purposes.

**Part-ML (Maintenance of light aircraft)**
: Part of the European continuing airworthiness regime applicable to light aircraft, including many sailplanes.

**Part-SAO (Sailplane Air Operations)**
: Part of Regulation (EU) 2018/1976 containing the operational requirements applicable to sailplanes.

**Part-SFCL (Sailplane Flight Crew Licensing)**
: Part of Regulation (EU) 2018/1976 governing sailplane licences, privileges, instructors and examiners.

**PIC (Pilot in Command)**
: The pilot designated as being in command and charged with the safe conduct of the flight.

**PPL (Private Pilot Licence)**
: Licence allowing the holder to exercise private pilot privileges under the applicable conditions.

**Prohibited area (P)**
: Airspace of defined dimensions, above the land areas or territorial waters of a State, within which the flight of aircraft is prohibited.

**QFE (Altimeter setting referred to aerodrome datum)**
: Setting that makes the altimeter show height relative to the datum for which it was calculated and, at that point, read approximately zero.

**QNE (Standard altimeter setting indication)**
: Indication obtained by setting 1013.25 hPa, used to express flight levels; it is not a pressure reported by a station.

**QNH (Altimeter setting to mean sea level)**
: Setting that lets the altimeter show altitude and, on the ground, approximately the elevation of the point considered.

**RCC (Rescue Coordination Centre)**
: Unit responsible for coordinating search and rescue operations within an assigned region.

**Restricted area (R)**
: Airspace of defined dimensions within which the flight of aircraft is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

**RMZ (Radio Mandatory Zone)**
: Airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and use of radio equipment is mandatory in accordance with the published requirements.

**RSC (Rescue Sub-Centre)**
: Unit subordinate to an RCC that coordinates search and rescue operations in part of its region.

**SAR (Search and Rescue)**
: Organisation and operations intended to locate and assist aircraft and persons in distress.

**SB (Service Bulletin)**
: Manufacturer's communication with instructions, inspections or modifications, whether mandatory or not depending on the applicable framework.

**SERA (Standardised European Rules of the Air)**
: Common rules of the air laid down by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 923/2012.

**SPIC (Student Pilot-in-Command)**
: Student pilot acting as pilot-in-command on a flight with an instructor who only observes and does not influence the control of the aircraft.

**SPL (Sailplane Pilot Licence)**
: European Union licence, governed by Part-SFCL, that allows the holder to exercise the privileges of a sailplane pilot under the applicable conditions.

**TMA (Terminal Control Area)**
: Control area normally established at the confluence of ATS routes in the vicinity of one or more major aerodromes, with the limits published for each TMA.

**TMG (Touring Motor Glider)**
: Powered sailplane with a non-retractable engine and propeller that can take off and climb under its own power.

**TMZ (Transponder Mandatory Zone)**
: Airspace in which the carriage and operation of a transponder with the required capabilities is mandatory; on its own it does not require radio communication or listening watch, unless it is also an RMZ or it is so published.

**TR (Type Rating)**
: Endorsement on the licence certifying the qualification to operate a type of aircraft when the rules require that rating.

**TRA (Temporary Reserved Area)**
: Volume of airspace temporarily reserved for a specific activity, through which other aircraft may be allowed to pass under the applicable conditions.

**TSA (Temporary Segregated Area)**
: Volume of airspace temporarily reserved and segregated from other traffic while it is active.

**TWR (Aerodrome Control Tower)**
: ATS unit established to provide control service to aerodrome traffic.

**VFR (Visual Flight Rules)**
: Rules applicable to flights conducted with visual references and within the corresponding weather and operating minima; the separation provided by ATC depends on the airspace class and the traffic involved.

**VMC (Visual Meteorological Conditions)**
: Visibility and distance-from-cloud conditions equal to or better than the applicable minima.

**VOR (VHF Omnidirectional Radio Range)**
: Radio navigation aid that provides magnetic radials relative to a ground station.
